title: Meaning of $$\sin(\theta)$$ in terms of the unit circle.
text: Recall that $$\sin(\theta)$$ is the $$y$$ coordinate of the point on the unit circle with radian angle $$\theta.$$

title: Find the location where $$y=-1$$
text: First we find the point on the circle whose $$y$$ coordinate is $$-1$$. That only happens at the lowest point on the circle, where the negative $$y-$$ axis intersects the unit circle.

title: Find all angles in $$(-3\pi, 3\pi).$$
text: We can add or subtract $$2\pi$$ from $$\frac{-\pi}{2}$$ and will be back at the same point.

title: Is that all of the angles?
text: If we add or subtract another $$2\pi$$ we will end up outside of the domain $$(-3\pi, 3\pi)$$ since $$\frac{-\pi}{2}-4\pi=\frac{-9\pi}{2}<-3\pi$$ and $$\frac{-\pi}{2}+4\pi=\frac{7\pi}{2}>3\pi.$$
